Cobo Wallet, One of the Early Crypto Wallet Apps Launched by F2Pool Co-Founder, to Shut Down Digital asset custody provider Cobo announced that its Cobo Wallet App will shut down on December 1 as part of a strategic business adjustment. Users must withdraw all assets by November 30 at 11:59 PM (UTC+8). Any remaining assets will incur a monthly management fee of 2%, with a minimum charge of $100. Accounts holding less than $100 will have their entire remaining balance deducted. The first fee will be charged on January 1, 2027, and fees will continue until all assets are withdrawn or depleted. Cobo emphasized that its other businesses will remain unaffected and continue operating normally. — link

Former Mt. Gox CEO: Ledger Received Hardware Wallet Tampering Reports Since December 2025 but Issued No Public Warning Former Mt. Gox CEO Mark Karpelès said Ledger had received reports of hardware wallets tampered with and fitted with malicious components since at least December 2025, but he had seen no subsequent public warning. Security researcher Joe Grand said he reported a compromised Nano X purchased through Lazada in Thailand on March 4, 2026, which Ledger acknowledged and said it was investigating internally. A security incident disclosed on October 9 involved devices sold by authorized Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis. Karpelès urged Ledger to warn users more proactively as similar reports increase and attacks grow more sophisticated. — link

Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 Cuts Quantum Circuit Gate Count for Elliptic-Curve Operations by 17x On October 16, Anthropic published research showing that Claude Mythos 5, assisted by an automated evaluation system, optimized eight quantum circuit design tasks spanning quantum chemistry, optimization, physics simulation, and number theory, producing new designs that outperform previously published methods. Claude developed a reversible modular inversion algorithm that eliminates the need to store branch history. One elliptic-curve point addition circuit uses approximately 17 times fewer quantum gates while requiring 12% more qubits. Another improvement reduced the gate count of Reed–Solomon decoding circuits in the quantum optimization algorithm DQI by approximately 12 times. The results remain at the quantum circuit design and verification stage and have not yet been validated on actual quantum hardware. — link

Highlight Clip: a16z Crypto Partner: Finance Remains Blockchain's Clearest Near-Term Application Opportunity a16z Crypto Partner: Finance Remains Blockchain's Clearest Near-Term Application Opportunity a16z Crypto General Partner Guy Wuollet said in an October 6 interview on the official a16z crypto channel that blockchain's clearest near-term opportunities remain in finance, particularly stablecoins and perpetuals. a16z is also focused on payments, lending, credit, exchanges, prediction markets, derivatives, crypto-AI, and wealth management. Wuollet said stablecoin demand is driven by payment efficiency and demand for U.S. dollars in high-inflation or capital-controlled markets. He sees stablecoins and blockchains as driving finance's digital transformation, much as cloud services transformed enterprise IT. — link
